title: Signal Runner: field notes for alert triage and cohort comparisons
content:
Purpose:
Quick-running notes from the nightly/early-morning runs where I exercise the new alert signals and compare two live cohorts (control vs. new-routing). This is a scratchpad used during triage runs and will evolve into formal playbook steps once we stabilize the checklist.

High-level hypothesis pattern I use when an alert spikes: 
1) Is this signal global or route-scoped? (check per-route panels first)
2) Did shape change (p50/p95/p99) or only the tail/variance?
3) Are token-paths/kv-cache hits correlated?
4) Are worker-level resource counters (GPU utilization, RT mem) changing?
5) Did routing/compile kernels change in last deploy window?

Quick dashboard checklist (order matters):
- Route overview: requests/sec, error-rate, p50/p95/p99 latency (last 1h vs. baseline 24h)
- Token accounting: tokens-per-request distribution, per-route token cost breakdown
- KV cache: hit-rate by model+route, eviction rate, cache occupancy by shard
- Batching: average batch size, queue-time, throttle events
- Resource telemetry: GPU util, CPU steal, IO wait, swap usage (if any)
- Canary cohorts: cohort A (control) vs cohort B (new-routing) side-by-side percentiles and sample traces

Useful PromQL snippets I run (copy-paste friendly):
- p95 latency per route: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~"$route"}[5m])) by (le))
- kv cache hit rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{model=~"$model"}[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{model=~"$model"}[5m]))
- batch queue time: avg_over_time(batch_queue_time_seconds{pool="$pool"}[5m])

Trace sampling approach:
- Increase sampling on impacted route (trace-sampler override) for 30 minutes.
- Pull 20 longest tail traces and 10 median traces from each cohort.
- Use trace playback tool to replay top-3 tail traces in local microbench with controlled token-length to reproduce.

Reproduction recipe I use locally (microbench):
- Recreate request headers + sequence length distribution using anonymized sample payloads.
- Run 100 synthetic calls to replicate observed batch and queue patterns.
- Toggle KV cache on/off to see delta in worker-side duration.
- If kernel-compile path suspected, pin model variant to previous image and compare.

Common root causes discovered in prior runs (notes):
- Regression A: small change in kernel scheduling bumped evicted KV entries causing extra forward passes — manifested as p99 spikes only on long token requests. (See SERV-3710)
- Regression B: routing policy introduced cross-region fanout for a small fraction of requests, increasing median queue-time and visible in per-worker queue-size heatmaps.
- Regression C: autoscaler cooldown misconfiguration led to transient underprovisioning during traffic bursts — visible as step-changes in queue-time with no increase in request rate.

Decision matrix for quick mitigation:
- If delta is >40% p95 and cohort B worse: rollback routing change or divert traffic back to control (fast rollback).
- If tail-only and related to long sequences: enable prefix-caching override and increase KV cache retention for affected model shard.
- If resources saturated across both cohorts: scale up pool, enable emergency-burst-capacity, and file infra incident.

Sample session from 2025-02-28 (actual triage timeline):
- 02:10: Alert fired: p99 latency for route "/chat/stream" +420ms (baseline: 900ms -> 1320ms).
- 02:12: Dashboard inspection: cohort B p50 ~ same, p95 +10%, p99 +46%. KV hit-rate for cohort B dropped from 88% -> 62% in last 20m.
- 02:20: Increased trace sampling + collected 25 traces. Playback reproduced 30–40ms extra per-token in forward path on cohort B.
- 02:35: Hypothesis: k-v cache churn due to newly-deployed eviction policy (PR #1284).
- 02:47: Mitigation: temporarily revert eviction setting via config flag; monitor.
- 03:05: p99 for cohort B back to baseline within 8 minutes. Follow-up: schedule deeper profiling with memory alloc traces.

Notes about canary comparisons that reduce noisy signals:
- Use fixed-window percentiles (rolling 5m vs rolling 1h) to avoid alarm fatigue from transient spikes.
- Normalize by tokens-per-request when comparing cohorts to make sure longer prompts don't bias p95.
- Always compare the same model-version image; if we want to evaluate a new image, pin other variables (traffic mix, sequence length).

Open questions / To-dos (short):
- Automate cohort-normalized dashboards that show per-token percentiles (Samir owns) — ticket SERV-4890.
- Add a lightweight A/B diff panel that highlights delta-only signals (percent change + confidence) — proposal needed.
- Investigate correlation between background GC pauses and tail latency on worker type g4dn-like machines.

Action items from this file: 
- [ ] Add a canned query for "kv-cache eviction churn" to the triage dashboard. (Owner: Marco)
- [ ] Create a small runbook for trace-playback reproduction to be shared with on-call (Owner: Priya).
- [ ] Post-run retrospective in #runtime-observability with summary and link to PR/rollback notes.

Meta: format & intended audience
- This is intentionally informal and acting as a daily lab notebook. Intended audience: SREs, serving eng, and applied ML folks who jump into night triage. When stable, we will condense into a proper runbook in Confluence and attach example queries and playback scripts.

Raw scratch snippets (logs / commands I used):
- curl -H 'X-Cohort: B' https://api.redwood.dev/chat/stream -d @sample-long.json --output /tmp/trace.raw
- python tools/playback.py --trace /tmp/trace.raw --iterations 10 --pin-model rwd-v1-7b
- psql perf_db -c "select time_bucket('1m', ts) as t, percentile_cont(0.95) within group (lat) as p95 from requests where route='/chat/stream' and cohort='B' and ts > now() - interval '1 hour' group by t order by t desc limit 60;"

If you use anything in here during an incident, please add a short note at the bottom with timestamp and outcome so we can iterate on the checklist.

-- Priya K.
